visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video begins with an outdoor scene showing a large promotional poster for the Animage and Studio Ghibli exhibition. The poster features iconic characters from Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind and My Neighbor Totoro. A person wearing a brown vest and a baseball cap stands to the left of the poster. The lighting is bright and natural, indicating a clear day. (2) The scene cuts to a digital display screen showing ticket prices, including a pre-sale price of $390. This is followed by a close-up of a hand holding a small white sticker featuring a character from Spirited Away against a white wall with the exhibition title. The camera uses a close-up shot to emphasize the tactile detail of the sticker. (3) Inside the exhibition, the characters walk through a blue-walled gallery filled with framed magazine spreads and original character designs. They observe various sketches, including detailed pencil drawings of Nausicaä on aged paper. The lighting is focused and warm, typical of an indoor gallery setting. Several other visitors can be seen in the background. (4) The visual narrative shifts to a showcase of vintage merchandise, including metal pencil cases and ticket stubs from past Ghibli film releases. A wall featuring a photo of a young Hayao Miyazaki playing with a kendama is shown, alongside a full-scale statue of Nausicaä in her blue pilot suit. The characters interact with the displays, showing facial expressions of curiosity and excitement. (5) The group moves to an interactive area where a large model of Laputa and a projection room for Grave of the Fireflies are displayed. They are then seen waving from inside a plush Catbus window and posing within a giant yellow frame that mimics an Animage magazine cover. The camera uses medium and wide shots to capture the scale of these installations. (6) The final sequence takes place in a bright gift shop filled with shelves of Ghibli-themed merchandise like bags, candles, and pins. The three main characters are then shown together in front of a poster wall, holding commemorative cards and smiling at the camera. The editing uses fast cuts to create a dynamic and energetic concluding rhythm.
